title: Time Bender
blurb: History's dates are messing with you. Three are real, one is cap. Trust nothing.

cards.say: Harvard University [was founded before anyone had invented calculus], [held its first graduation, for nine students, the year Galileo died], [was founded before William Shakespeare died], and [is named after a minister who left it his library].
cards.real: Shakespeare died in 1616. Harvard was founded 20 years later, in 1636, by a vote of the Massachusetts Bay Colony's legislature.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Harvard_University (named Harvard College in 1639 for John Harvard, who willed it his library of some 400 books)

cards.say: The Ottoman Empire [still existed when Mickey Mouse first appeared in a cartoon], [lasted for more than six centuries], [conquered Constantinople almost 40 years before Columbus sailed], and [still existed when the Wright brothers first flew].
cards.real: The Ottoman sultanate was abolished in November 1922, six years before Mickey Mouse's first cartoons came out in 1928.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Ottoman_Empire (empire lasted to 1922; Wright brothers flew December 1903, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_brothers)

cards.say: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart [is younger than America's Liberty Bell], [wrote music for a glass instrument invented by Benjamin Franklin], [was still alive when George Washington became president], and [wrote the tune of Twinkle Twinkle Little Star at age five].
cards.real: The tune is an older French song from around 1765. Mozart wrote 12 variations on it in 1781 or 1782, in his twenties, so he gets the credit.
src: https://www.themorgan.org/exhibitions/online/mozart/418 (variations K. 265 written in Vienna 1781-1782 on a tune by an unknown composer from around 1765)

cards.say: Marie Curie [was born the same year the United States bought Alaska], [won her second Nobel Prize after World War I ended], [won her first Nobel Prize the same year the Wright brothers first flew], and [set up mobile X-ray units for soldiers in World War I].
cards.real: Curie's second Nobel Prize, in chemistry, came in 1911, three years before World War I began. She was the first person ever to win two.
src: https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/marie-curie/facts (Chemistry prize 1911, first person to win two)
https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/marie-curie/facts (organized mobile X-ray teams in World War I)

cards.say: Charles Darwin [was born on the very same day as Abraham Lincoln], [died before Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone], [ate puma, armadillo and iguana on his voyage around the world], and [published his theory of evolution before the US Civil War began].
cards.real: Bell patented the telephone in 1876. Darwin lived six more years and died in April 1882.
src: https://www.nhpr.org/npr-blogs/2015-08-12/dining-like-darwin-when-scientists-swallow-their-subjects (puma, armadillos and iguanas on the Beagle voyage)
https://clarklibrary.ucla.edu/blog/charles-darwin-abraham-lincoln-and-the-12th-of-february/ (On the Origin of Species, 1859; the Civil War began April 1861)

cards.say: Apple [was founded before the first Star Wars movie came out], [was founded closer in time to the Moon landing than to the first iPhone], [had a third co-founder who sold his 10 percent share for 800 dollars], and [got its start a year before its rival Microsoft did].
cards.real: Microsoft was founded in April 1975 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, a year before Apple started on April 1, 1976.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. (founded April 1, 1976; Star Wars opened May 25, 1977)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. (founded 1976: 7 years after the July 1969 Moon landing, 31 years before the 2007 iPhone)

cards.say: Nokia [made the world's first mobile phone call, back in 1973], [started out as a pulp mill before the telephone was even invented], [was once the third-biggest TV maker in Europe], and [got its classic ringtone from a guitar piece older than the airplane].
cards.real: The first mobile phone call was made by Martin Cooper of Motorola in 1973. Nokia's first mobile phone, the Mobira Senator car phone, came in 1982.
src: https://www.aarp.org/politics-society/history/info-2018/first-cell-phone-call.html (Motorola's Martin Cooper, 1973) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia (first mobile phone, Mobira Senator, 1982)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia_tune (Tarrega's Gran Vals, 1902; the Wright brothers first flew December 1903)

cards.say: The Mongol Empire [was founded nine years before England's Magna Carta], [is about a century older than the Ottoman Empire], [took over Japan after invading it in 1281], and [had more than 1,400 postal relay stations in China alone].
cards.real: The Mongols invaded Japan in 1274 and 1281 and failed both times. In 1281 a huge typhoon wrecked much of their fleet.
src: https://www.britannica.com/facts/Genghis-Khan (khan of the Mongol empire from 1206; Magna Carta was sealed in 1215)
https://historyofinformation.com/detail.php?id=3043 (more than 1,400 postal stations in China under Kublai Khan)

cards.say: Galileo Galilei [was born the same year as William Shakespeare], [was still alive when the Pilgrims landed at Plymouth], [has one of his fingers on display in a museum in Florence], and [built the world's very first telescope in 1608].
cards.real: A Dutch eyeglass maker, Hans Lippershey, tried to patent a telescope in 1608. Galileo heard about it and built his own better one in 1609.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_Galilei (died 8 January 1642; the Mayflower Pilgrims landed in 1620)

cards.say: The Beatles [released their first single on the day the first James Bond movie premiered], [hit number one in Britain with their very first single], [gave their final public performance before the first Moon landing], and [had the police come up to stop their final show].
cards.real: Love Me Do, their first single, came out in October 1962 and peaked at number 17 on the UK chart.
src: https://blog.oup.com/2012/10/beatles-friday-5-october-1962-love-me-do/ (Love Me Do issued and Dr. No premiered on 5 October 1962)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles%27_rooftop_concert (30 January 1969, final public performance; Apollo 11 landed July 20, 1969)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles%27_rooftop_concert (Metropolitan Police officers came to stop the performance)

cards.say: Johann Sebastian Bach [was born the same year as the composer Handel], [died less than six years before Mozart was born], [was born after Isaac Newton published his laws of motion], and [had 20 children with his two wives].
cards.real: Bach was born in March 1685. Newton's Principia, with his laws of motion, came out two years later, in July 1687.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Sebastian_Bach (seven children with Maria Barbara, 13 with Anna Magdalena)

cards.say: Jackie Robinson [played his first big-league game before World War II ended], [broke baseball's color line before the US Air Force existed], [won the first Rookie of the Year award baseball ever handed out], and [had his number 42 retired by every MLB team in 1997].
cards.real: World War II ended in 1945. Robinson, who served in the Army during the war, played his first game for the Brooklyn Dodgers on April 15, 1947.
src: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Jackie-Robinson (Army 1942 to 1944, debut April 15, 1947; World War II ended in 1945)
https://wiki.riteme.site/wiki/1947_in_the_United_States (Robinson's debut April 15; the Air Force became a separate branch in September 1947)
https://www.britannica.com/biography/Jackie-Robinson (MLB's inaugural Rookie of the Year award, 1947)
https://www.britannica.com/biography/Jackie-Robinson (number 42 retired for all of MLB in April 1997)
